entries.name: strictify_weak_certificate
entries.note: Finite-cube perturbation. Preserve the topology and numerators. For every weakly oriented legal denominator choose a strict direction with the same orientation (positiveDirection for nonnegative slopes; for nonpositive slopes use an affine form with slopes -1 and a sufficiently large positive constant). Perturb all finitely many denominators by one sufficiently small positive parameter. Prove legality and strict orientation coefficientwise. Use finiteness/continuity, or explicit denominator and score margins on Cube n, to choose the parameter so every represented truth-table sign is unchanged.

entries.name: fracComputable_hasCanonicalCertificate
entries.note: Reuse the construction and proof of fracComputable_hasCertificate in FracAtomBridge.lean. Its denominators are fracDenominator φ with slope ρ_i*(α-1); hρ and hα imply all slopes have one weak common sign, with the only non-strict case α=1. Package the same Certificate, establish WeaklyOriented for every denominator by cases α≤1/1≤α, and invoke strictify_weak_certificate without changing topology or budget. Handle H=0 exactly as the relaxed bridge does.

entries.name: exists_hasCanonicalCertificate
entries.note: Copy the totality pattern of exists_hasCertificate: obtain H and computableWithHeadsN from HeadComplexity.exists_computable, convert with computableWithHeadsN_iff_fracComputable, then apply fracComputable_hasCanonicalCertificate and return budget H.

entries.name: POIC2_le_HStar
entries.note: Unfold the minimality interface only through POIC2_le_of_hasCanonicalCertificate. Obtain fracComputable n (HStar n f) f from HStar_eq_Lfrac/Nat.find or the existing HStar specification lemmas used in FracAtomBridge, feed it to fracComputable_hasCanonicalCertificate, and conclude at the same budget.

entries.name: theorem026_exists_hard_function
entries.note: Use theorem026_counting_lower_bound. If every BoolFn n lay in the HStar sublevel, that finite set would have cardinal 2^(2^n). The assumed strict exponent inequality gives 2^(64*n^2*H) < 2^(2^n), contradiction. Reuse Fintype.card_congr/card_fun/card_bool and sublevel membership lemmas; finish by classical finite-set cardinality and omega/norm_num arithmetic.

entries.name: exists_spanningBank
entries.note: Use the already formalized powerBlockLocalization construction. For n≥2 take its fixed family of positive strict denominators, and use LocalizationMatrix/Lagrange interpolation to express an arbitrary real table with affine numerators over those poles. Handle n=0 and n=1 explicitly with one legal denominator. The result only needs existence of some finite H, not an optimal count.

entries.name: HStar_le_Bank
entries.note: Take the minimal spanning bank and apply FixedBankSpans to the signed table v(x)=if f x then 1 else -1. Convert each quotient A_h/B_h with B_h.StrictAdmissible to one FracAtom. Positive slopes use exists_fracAtom_eval_eq; for negative common slopes prove the analogous construction with 0<α<1 (or complement the Boolean variables). Sum gives fracComputable n (Bank n) f with bias 0, then use HStar_le_of_fracComputable.

entries.name: spanningBank_dimension_bound
entries.note: Fix B from HasSpanningBank. For each h the map AffineForm n → (Cube n→ℝ), A ↦ A.eval/B_h.eval is linear and has range dimension at most n+1. All ranges contain the same constant table 1 (take A=B_h), so the sum of H ranges has dimension at most 1+n*H, not merely H*(n+1). FixedBankSpans makes their sum equal the full table space, whose real finrank is Fintype.card (Cube n)=2^n. Formalize with LinearMap.range, Submodule.finrank_sup_le, and the common one-dimensional intersection.

entries.name: bank_lower_bound
entries.note: Start from bank_dimension_bound n: 2^n ≤ 1+n*Bank n. Under 1≤n derive 2^n-1 ≤ n*Bank n and prove the explicit Nat ceiling inequality ((2^n-1)+(n-1))/n ≤ Bank n. Search Mathlib Nat ceil-division lemmas; omega plus Nat.div_le_iff_le_mul is likely enough.

entries.name: bank_le_powerBlock_groupCount
entries.note: Construct HasSpanningBank n (powerBlockLocalization n hn).groupCount from the existing power-block denominators and localization inverse. This is the uniform-in-v strengthening of the existing per-function Headline proof: keep the poles fixed, let interpolation numerators depend linearly on the arbitrary table v, and package StrictAdmissible using the established PositiveCoefficients/strict legality lemmas.

entries.name: bank_pow_two
entries.note: Combine bank_lower_bound for n=2^m with bank_le_powerBlock_groupCount and the exact groupCount/cardinality computation for powerBlockLocalization at power-of-two arity. Under 1≤m, n divides 2^n and the explicit ceiling equals 2^n/n. Use Nat.pow_pos, pow divisibility and omega after rewriting the localization groupCount.

entries.name: bank_one
entries.note: Lower bound follows from bank_dimension_bound 1. For the upper bound give one explicit strict legal affine denominator on one bit (for example constant 2, slope 1) and solve the two values of any v by an affine numerator A; then apply Bank_le_of_hasSpanningBank.

entries.name: f8_thresholdDegLE_two
entries.note: Reuse the quadratic distance polynomial for distThreshold 4 from DistanceThreshold.lean. The polynomial Σ_i (x_i+y_i-2*x_i*y_i) - 3/2 strictly sign-represents hammingDist≥2 on Boolean vertices and has totalDegree≤2. Prefer existing general distThreshold threshold-degree upper lemmas.

entries.name: f8_not_thresholdDegLE_one
entries.note: Use a two-coordinate checkerboard restriction with the other six bits fixed so the four restricted labels are XOR/equality in the non-linearly-separable pattern. Apply the affine rectangle identity: values at 00 and 11 sum to values at 01 and 10, contradicting the required strict signs. Reuse existing DistanceThreshold lower-bound/checkerboard lemmas if available.

entries.name: thresholdDeg_f8
entries.note: Use f8_thresholdDegLE_two for ≤2 and f8_not_thresholdDegLE_one for not ≤1. Unfold thresholdDeg only through existing minimality/specification lemmas. Rule out 0 and 1 and conclude equality by omega.

entries.name: f8_quadratic_mixed_negative
entries.note: Multilinearize P on the Boolean cube without increasing degree. Let K=mixedMatrix4 P. For every nonzero real z, derive zᵀ sym(K) z<0 from the strict signs on Hamming balls of radius 0/1 versus distance≥2, using checkerboard second differences and polarization; pure-left, pure-right, affine and constant terms cancel. It is acceptable to add proved helper lemmas for coefficient extraction, Boolean multilinear evaluation and the finite four-dimensional curvature identity.

entries.name: columnMax_spectral_inequality
entries.note: Unpack d>0 with S=diagonal d * M symmetric and PositiveIndexAtLeastTwo4 S. Positive row sums of M give a positive test direction. Prove the four-dimensional trace/column-max inequality by contradiction: if trace M + 2*max_{i≠j} M_ij≤0 in every column, establish that the symmetrized form has positive index at most one, contradicting the supplied two-dimensional positive subspace. The conclusion uses an existential off-diagonal picker, so choose actual Finset maximizers after proving the max form.

entries.name: two_heads_yield_f8NormalizedSystem
entries.note: Unfold computableWithHeadsN via computableWithHeadsN_iff_fracComputable. Clear the two positive affine denominators, multilinearize the resulting quadratic sign polynomial, and apply f8_quadratic_mixed_negative. Normalize coefficients to the paper variables U,V,w,μ. Verify exactly the fields of F8NormalizedSystem: U+Uᵀ positive definite, V inertia (2,2), strict diagonal/contraction inequalities from all radius-0/1 vertices, positive left/right slopes, isotropic null equation, and intercept inequality. Add small algebraic helpers rather than changing the structure.

entries.name: not_nonempty_f8NormalizedSystem
entries.note: Assume a normalized system. Apply the column-max spectral inequality to the matrix arising from the U,V normalization (prove its positive diagonal symmetrizability and two-positive-index property from V_inertia and slope data). Sum the contraction inequalities at the chosen off-diagonal maximizers. Combine with null/intercept and positive slope fields to obtain the opposite nonpositive trace-plus-column-max bound. Finish by linarith/Finset sum rearrangement.

entries.name: f8_denominators_admissible
entries.note: All listed slopes are strictly negative, so StrictlyOriented is immediate by fin_cases/norm_num. For StrictLegal, each denominator constant exceeds the sum of absolute negative slopes: D1 34>20, D2 31>30, D3 32>26. Expand AffineForm.eval and bound bitReal in {0,1}; because there are only Fin 8 coordinates, fin_cases and norm_num/simp is acceptable.

entries.name: f8_integer_certificate_margin
entries.note: This is an exact 256-vertex finite audit of the published integer certificate. Unfold f8, f8ClearedScore, all six affine forms, integerAffine8, AffineForm.eval, boolSign, hammingDist/leftBits/rightBits. Prove by exhaustive fin_cases on the eight Bool coordinates followed by norm_num/decide/simp. native_decide is forbidden, but ordinary decide, norm_num and explicit finite case splitting are allowed. The exact minimum signed cleared margin is 58.

entries.name: f8_computableWithHeadsN_three
entries.note: Use the three explicit quotients A_i/D_i plus global bias 1. From f8_denominators_admissible construct one FracAtom for each affine quotient; handle strictly negative slopes by choosing a common 0<α<1 and positive ρ_i, solving γ,η,m,δ exactly (the positive-slope converse exists_fracAtom_eval_eq is a template). Denominators are positive, so f8_integer_certificate_margin and multiplication by D1*D2*D3 prove the required strict sign equivalence. Convert fracComputable 8 3 f8 to computableWithHeadsN.

entries.name: HStar_f8
entries.note: Upper bound 3 comes from f8_computableWithHeadsN_three and the HStar minimality lemma. Lower bound follows from f8_not_computableWithHeadsN_two plus monotonicity/minimality: if HStar≤2, obtain a two-head realization (padding fewer heads if necessary) and contradict it. Finish by omega.
